changes.summary: DOJ arrested a government contractor and filed a criminal complaint alleging unlawful transmission of national-defense information to a journalist.
changes.duplicate_review: No canonical event, normalized title, primary URL or recent pull request matched. The same-day Floris/Benavides complaints concern different defendants, statutes, evidence and alleged conduct.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: DOJ announced that the FBI arrested Ian A. Brinksman after searching his Washington residence and charged him by criminal complaint under 18 U.S.C. § 793(d). The release says he held TS/SCI access and repeats officials' national-security rationale while expressly stating that complaint charges are allegations and the defendant is presumed innocent.
source_inspections.hash_scope: SHA-256 of the exact normalized evidence extract retained here; the downloaded release HTML separately hashed to d1720ebf76a91c2c5c37d68aa58c64dd4a385c1299f487a4db7428d5db015ede.

source_inspections.origin_group: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia
source_inspections.evidence_extract: The 13-page affidavit in EDVA case 1:26-mj-423 states that it is offered only to establish probable cause. It alleges five access-and-publication sequences using classified database logs, badge records, calls, emails and classification review, and says the reports were outside Brinksman's work scope.

source_inspections.evidence_extract: Reuters reported the October 23 arrest and search, identified the journalist as Aída Chávez, summarized the affidavit's five alleged disclosure sequences and reported that Brinksman's federal public defender declined comment while Chávez, Deloitte and the State Department had not immediately responded.
